bull.b: TSMC’s concentration in advanced nodes supports durable pricing power, customer relevance, and scale advantages in high-performance computing and AI. The strong mix also reinforces its technological lead and creates a platform for continued demand as customers migrate to newer process generations.

Very high operating and net margins indicate substantial manufacturing scale, strong execution, and customer willingness to pay for differentiated process technology. These economics provide internal funding for research and capacity expansion while strengthening resilience across the semiconductor cycle.

bull.t: Strong Balance Sheet And Cash Generation
bull.b: Low relative leverage and rising operating cash flow give TSMC financial flexibility to fund its large technology roadmap without relying excessively on external financing. Strong cash generation also supports dividends, overseas expansion, and investment through changing industry conditions.

bear.b: The overseas manufacturing build-out and steep 2nm ramp are expected to reduce gross margins over the coming years. Although these investments support strategic customer proximity and capacity, the transition may temporarily pressure profitability before new fabs achieve mature utilization and yields.

TSMC’s expansion requires exceptionally high capital commitments for leading-edge fabs, packaging, and global capacity. Management expects revenue to outpace CapEx, but the investment cycle still lowers free-cash-flow conversion and increases execution demands across multiple construction and technology ramps.

TSMC remains exposed to uneven end-market demand, particularly where consumers are price-sensitive, while shortages in back-end capacity can constrain shipments even when wafer demand is strong. These factors can create revenue volatility and complicate the timing of growth across product platforms.
